short: HES1-7, HEY1/2, HEYL and HELT are the vertebrate hairy/Enhancer-of-split relatives: bHLH repressors with an Orange domain that sets partner choice and a C-terminal WRPW or YRPW peptide that recruits TLE/Groucho corepressors. Most are direct Notch targets, so their activity reports Notch signalling. They read a genuinely different site from the class II bHLH activators — a proline in the basic region shifts preference away from CANNTG. Two sites are described: the functionally defined N box CACNAG, and the higher-affinity CACGYG (CACGTG or CACGCG) that the database matrices actually capture. HES1 autorepression through N boxes generates a two-hour expression oscillation; HES7 drives the somite segmentation clock.
long:
## The factors

HES1-HES7, HEY1, HEY2, HEYL and HELT are the vertebrate relatives of *Drosophila* hairy and Enhancer of split, and they are structurally distinct from the class I and class II bHLH proteins that read E-boxes. Three features define them. First, a proline in the basic region, which is why this group is sometimes called the proline-bHLH class and why its sequence preference differs from CANNTG [PMID:12548545]. Second, an Orange domain, a two-helix module immediately C-terminal to the bHLH that restricts which partners a given member will dimerise with. Third, a C-terminal tetrapeptide — WRPW in HES proteins, YRPW in HEY proteins — that recruits TLE/Groucho corepressors [PMID:17586813]. They are repressors, not activators. Most are direct transcriptional targets of Notch signalling through RBPJ/CSL, so their expression reports Notch activity [PMID:17329370]: HES1 broadly, HES5 in neural progenitors, HES7 in presomitic mesoderm, HEY1/HEY2/HEYL in cardiovascular and endothelial tissue. HES2, HES3, HES4 and HES6 are divergent; HES6 does not behave like a canonical repressor [PMID:17329370]. Crucially, these proteins repress by two routes. They bind DNA and recruit corepressors, and they also sequester class II activators: HES1 reduces E47-driven transcription and blocks MyoD- and MASH1-driven differentiation, which requires no HES site at all [PMID:8524259].

## The motif

Two different sites are attributed to this family, and the distinction matters. The site defined functionally is the N box, CACNAG, the Enhancer-of-split recognition sequence through which HES1 represses transcription [PMID:1340473]. *Drosophila* hairy was then shown to prefer a non-canonical site, CACGCG, and mutating a single CACGCG in the *achaete* promoter abolishes hairy-mediated repression in cells and produces ectopic sensory organs in flies [PMID:7958930,7958929]. Different papers call this site a class C site or a class B E-box; the nomenclature is not consistent, so it is safer to write the sequence than the class name.

What the databases contain is neither of these. Twenty-four of the 26 motifs assigned here read CACGTG or CACGYG, usually with GG/CC flanks: GGCACGTGCC. The representative model is JASPAR HEY1 MA0823.1 (CACGTGCC), and almost all the HOCOMOCO models carry in vitro evidence (`S` or `SM`), so this is a real binding preference measured in vitro, not an artefact. Genome-wide, HEY1, HEY2 and HEYL bound preferentially to CACGYG, but a large fraction of efficiently bound promoters contained no E-box at all, implying additional, loosely defined binding modes [PMID:22615585]. The honest summary is that the high-affinity in vitro site is CACGYG, the classical repression site is the lower-affinity N box CACNAG, and the database matrices capture only the former. The atlas's data consensus CACGTGCC therefore disagrees with the ontology definition's N box for a documented reason rather than by error.

CACGTG is a problem sequence. It is the canonical palindromic E-box of MYC/MAX, USF1/2, TFE3/TFEB/MITF, SREBF1/2, BHLHE40/41, ARNT and the CLOCK-BMAL1 heterodimer. The Vierstra archetype `AC0068:HEY/CLOCK:bHLH` states this in its name. Two further Vierstra archetypes here, `AC0263:HES` and `AC0264:HES`, have low-information consensuses (CACACTT, CNCACGT) that resemble nothing else in the family and should not be used as HES models. Two CIS-BP entries, for HES4 and HEYL, are inferred from mouse proteins at 91% DNA-binding-domain identity.

## Where it acts

Unlike the E-box families, HES/HEY sites are promoter-proximal. Chromatin immunoprecipitation of HEY factors in HEK293 cells, cardiomyocytes and mouse hearts found binding clustered in proximal promoter regions, disproportionately at genes encoding transcriptional regulators and developmental control proteins [PMID:22615585]. CACGTG contains a CpG, so these sites are enriched in CpG islands and their occupancy is sensitive to DNA methylation. HES1 binds N boxes in its own promoter, and that negative feedback loop, combined with short protein and mRNA half-lives, generates a roughly two-hour oscillation in HES1 expression [PMID:12399594]. Neighbouring RBPJ/CSL sites are common, because these genes and their targets are Notch-responsive.

## Biology and disease

HES and HEY proteins are the main transcriptional output of Notch signalling. Hes1 and Hes5 maintain neural progenitors and delay neuronal differentiation; removing them causes premature neurogenesis and progenitor depletion [PMID:10205173]. Hes7 drives the segmentation clock in presomitic mesoderm, and its loss disorganises somite formation [PMID:11641270]; in humans, *HES7* mutations cause spondylocostal dysostosis with vertebral and rib malformations [PMID:23897666]. HEY1, HEY2 and HEYL are strikingly redundant, which is why single knockouts are often mild and combined losses phenocopy each other in the heart [PMID:22615585]. HES1 acts downstream of activated NOTCH1 in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia.

## Reading a hit

A CACGTG hit is one of the least specific results a scan can return: on sequence alone it is compatible with at least eight other families, several of which (MYC/MAX, USF, MITF, CLOCK-BMAL1) are far more abundantly expressed in most cell types than HES or HEY. Treat a CACGTG match as a "class B E-box" hit and resolve it with expression and co-factor evidence, not with motif scores. If you are specifically after Notch-effector repression, the functionally validated site is the N box CACNAG, which the database matrices will not find for you; scan for it separately and expect weak scores. The individual HES and HEY paralogues cannot be distinguished. Finally, remember that these proteins can repress without binding DNA, by titrating E-proteins and class II activators, so the absence of a site is not evidence that HES or HEY is not acting on a gene.
caveats: The site the databases model, CACGTG, is the canonical palindromic E-box shared with MYC/MAX, USF1/2, TFE3/TFEB/MITF, SREBF, BHLHE40/41, ARNT and CLOCK-BMAL1 — one Vierstra archetype here is named HEY/CLOCK for exactly that reason — so a hit is weak evidence for HES or HEY specifically. The classically defined repression site, the N box CACNAG, is lower affinity and is not represented by these matrices, so a scan will miss it. Two low-information Vierstra HES archetypes resemble nothing else in the family. HES4 and HEYL models are inferred from mouse proteins. HES and HEY also repress without binding DNA, by sequestering E-proteins, so absent sites do not exclude their involvement.

timeline.finding: Mammalian HES1 and HES3 are cloned as relatives of Drosophila hairy and Enhancer of split; HES1 represses through the N box CACNAG and separately reduces E-box-driven activation by E47 without binding that site, defining the two repression modes at the outset.
timeline.methods: cDNA cloning, gel shift and reporter assays
timeline.open: The relative importance of DNA-bound repression and activator sequestration in vivo.

timeline.finding: Drosophila hairy is shown to be a sequence-specific repressor that prefers the non-canonical site CACGCG rather than the N box, and mutating a single CACGCG in the achaete promoter abolishes repression in cells and produces ectopic sensory organs in flies — direct genetic evidence tying one site to one phenotype.
timeline.methods: binding-site selection, cell reporter assays, transgenic flies
timeline.open: Whether vertebrate HES proteins share the CACGCG preference or use the N box.

timeline.finding: Domain swaps place repression specificity outside the bHLH: the bHLH and Orange domains antagonise specific activators such as Scute, while the C-terminal WRPW tetrapeptide represses through corepressor recruitment, so two separable mechanisms operate.
timeline.methods: chimeric proteins assayed in Drosophila sex determination

timeline.finding: Hes1 and Hes5 are established as the Notch effectors that hold neural progenitors undifferentiated, with premature neurogenesis and progenitor depletion on their loss.

Dynamic rather than static repression emerges: Hes7 is shown to be required for ordered somite segmentation (2001), and Hes1 is shown to oscillate with a roughly two-hour period driven by negative autoregulation through N boxes in its own promoter plus short mRNA and protein half-lives (2002).
timeline.methods: mouse mutants, serum-synchronised cultures, mathematical modelling
timeline.open: Whether oscillation depends on the precise affinity of the autoregulatory N boxes.

timeline.finding: Genome-wide mapping of HEY1, HEY2 and HEYL finds binding clustered in proximal promoters of transcriptional regulators, a clear preference for class B E-boxes CACGYG rather than the N box, extensive redundancy among the three proteins, and many efficiently bound promoters with no E-box at all.
timeline.methods: ChIP-chip/ChIP-seq and microarray profiling in cells, cardiomyocytes and mouse heart
timeline.open: What the factors recognise at the E-box-free promoters was left undefined.

timeline.finding: HES7 mutation is shown to cause spondylocostal dysostosis in a large human family, carrying the segmentation-clock mechanism into human skeletal disease.
timeline.methods: linkage and sequencing in an extended family

open: Which site this family actually uses is unsettled: repression was defined functionally through the N box CACNAG and, in Drosophila, through CACGCG, whereas the in vitro matrices in these databases read CACGTG/CACGYG, and it is unresolved whether the N box is a genuine lower-affinity site used in vivo or an early assignment that the newer binding data supersede.

A large fraction of promoters efficiently bound by HEY proteins contain no E-box, and whether that reflects tethering by other DNA-binding factors, a degenerate site that position weight matrices do not capture, or indirect ChIP signal has not been determined.

How much HES/HEY repression requires DNA binding at all is unquantified: these proteins also repress by sequestering E-proteins and class II activators, a mode that needs no site, and the in vivo balance between the two mechanisms is unknown.

No paralogue-level sequence difference has been demonstrated within the family, and the two low-information Vierstra archetypes grouped here, AC0263:HES (CACACTT) and AC0264:HES (CNCACGT), resemble neither the CACGYG models nor each other, so whether they capture any real HES binding mode is doubtful.
